planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Romeo's new growth emerges coppery bronze before settling into its gold-edged variegated pattern, so afternoon shade helps prevent leaf scorch on the lighter margins.

directions: Romeo is a patented variegated Ternstroemia selection with dark green leaf centers edged in a broad band of buttery yellow to gold, deepening to a rosy-pink blush through the cooler months for a shifting, three-season color display uncommon among broadleaf shade shrubs. New spring growth flushes coppery bronze before settling into the mature variegated pattern, and small fragrant white flowers in late spring give way to ornamental black fruit. It shares the parent species' excellent tolerance of shade, humidity, and periods of both wet and dry soil, along with strong resistance to pests, disease, and deer browsing. Site it as a bright accent, informal screen, or foundation planting where its variegation can stand out against darker evergreens, and give it only occasional shaping since it holds a naturally dense, upright form.

common_name: Crown Jewels Ternstroemia (Red New-Growth Marbled Cleyera)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Crown Jewels grows larger than most variegated Ternstroemia selections, so give it room to develop into a substantial upright screen or specimen.

directions: Crown Jewels is a branch-mutation selection of Ternstroemia discovered in a Louisiana nursery, prized for bold red new growth that fades to bronze and then matures into dark green foliage marbled with grey and trimmed in a yellow-to-gold edge, giving it more dramatic seasonal color shifts than the plain-green species. White flowers appear from late spring into early summer on a dense, upright-growing plant that eventually reaches small-tree proportions in favorable sites. Like other Ternstroemia selections it thrives in partial to full shade, tolerates both moist and moderately dry soil once established, and shrugs off the pest and disease problems that trouble photinia and ligustrum in humid Gulf South landscapes. Use it as a specimen, tall screen, or background planting where its size and vivid new growth can be fully appreciated, and prune only lightly to maintain its naturally tidy upright habit.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in evenly moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade to part sun with protection from harsh winter wind; LeAnn is among the largest Ternstroemia selections, so reserve it for privacy screening or mass planting rather than tight foundation beds.

directions: LeAnn is a large, fast-growing Ternstroemia selection whose foliage cycles through color over the year: maroon leaves emerge in spring, mature to deep green through summer, and shift back to maroon again in fall and winter, giving year-round interest beyond the typical single spring flush of new growth. Fragrant white blooms appear in late spring and are followed by ornamental red berries in fall. It reaches a notably larger mature size than most Ternstroemia cultivars, making it well suited to living privacy screens, tall informal hedges, or mass plantings rather than small foundation beds, though it also responds well to formal shearing if a clipped hedge is wanted. It shares the species' drought tolerance once established, shade adaptability, and freedom from serious pests and disease, but performs poorly in heavy, poorly drained, or constantly wet soil.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; Hunny Bun stays far more compact than typical Ternstroemia selections, making it useful in foundation beds and containers where the species and its larger cultivars would quickly outgrow the space.

directions: Hunny Bun is a genuine dwarf Ternstroemia selection that forms a dense, rounded mound only about 4 feet tall and wide at maturity, a fraction of the size of the straight species and most other named cultivars in the genus. New foliage emerges a warm coppery bronze before maturing to glossy deep green, and small purple-tinted flowers appear in summer without significant ornamental impact. Its naturally tidy, compact habit needs little to no shearing to stay in bounds, making it a low-maintenance choice for small foundation beds, mixed borders, or containers where full-sized cleyera selections would be impractical. Like other Ternstroemia selections it tolerates heat, humidity, and considerable shade, and is largely free of serious pest and disease problems once established.

planting.note: Plant container specimens in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade; give Fortune's Cleyera protection from harsh afternoon sun, which can scorch the pale leaf margins, and from drying winter winds.

directions: Fortune's Cleyera is a long-cultivated variegated selection of true Cleyera japonica, first introduced from Japan in the 1860s and grown only in its variegated form ever since, with no known plain-green counterpart. Its leaves carry a cream-to-yellow margin around a deep green center, with new growth flushed pink before settling into the mature pattern, and the leaf edges take on a red flush in winter for added seasonal interest. Like the species, it bears small, fragrant, creamy-white flowers in late spring followed by red berries, and grows slowly into a refined, long-lived accent shrub for shaded woodland gardens. It performs best in partial to full shade with consistent moisture and humus-rich soil, since strong sun and dry conditions dull the variegation and can scorch the lighter leaf margins. Use it as a specimen or in a shaded border among camellias and azaleas, where its brighter foliage provides contrast to darker evergreens, and prune only lightly since it rarely needs correction.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)
